newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bond yields ticked higher in late trade on Wednesday after a lack of follow-through demand stymied the market's initial attempt to move below technical resistance around the 14.67 percent level.
At 1410 GMT, the key R150 was pegged at a 14.755 percent from 14.70 late on Tuesday.

The market initially took its cue from strength on the U.S. Treasury bond market where the 30-year T-bond moved to a 6.98 percent yield in New York overnight in the wake of inflation benign data released on Tuesday afternoon.
Early buying pushed the R150 to an intraday low of 14.66 percent where it bounced on a lack of follow-through buying and as players squared positions ahead of Thursday's market holiday.
"The market looked like it was going to break lower, but there was no follow-through and the longs had to sell off their positions," a trader said.

Dealers said institutions had also been sellers on the day, while foreigners continued to buy the market, albeit to a lesser extent than the last two days, after Deutsche Bank announced it had upped its 30-year bond by 500 million rand.
In the early afternoon, the market hovered around the 14.72 level until the release of latest U.S. GDP data at 1230 GMT.

The data showed the U.S. economy swelled by an annualised 5.6 percent in the first quarter compared with Wall Street economists' calls for a 4.1 percent rise, triggering renewed fears that the Federal Reserve might still have to hike U.S. interest rates later next month.
As a result, the U.S. Treasury bond lost ground to trade at 7.04 percent before retracing later to around the 7.01 mark.
Local traders also noted that much of the trade on the day had been influenced by options books ahead of Friday's noon close-out.
"A lot of trade is being influenced by the options books and we should see a lot more on Friday," a trader said, adding that strike looked likely to be set at 14.75 percent.
Bond Exchange figures show foreigners were net buyers of 734.94 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 679.9 million rand's worth on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 10.1 billion rand from 8.18 billion rand previously.
On the currency market, the rand was trading slightly weaker after maintaining its recent tight range for most of the day.
At 1400 GMT, it was quoted at 4.4450/4480 against the dollar from 4.4415/4445 late on Tuesday.
"We traded in a range all day and there was not much volumes," a trader said.
The main flows on the day stemmed from importer demand for dollars, which dealers said slightly outweighed offshore dollar selling.
Trade on Friday was expected to be extremely thin as many players were taking a long weekend.
Next week, the currency was expected to trade in a 4.43 to 4.46 range.

Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.5107/5525 yen from 28.5312/5730 yen on Tuesday, at 0.3893/3897 marks from 0.3887/3891 marks previously and at 7.2070/2163 against sterling from 7.2337/2431.
Major banks kept their three month deposit rates steady at between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage rose to 8.935 billion rand on Tuesday from 8.372 billion rand on Saturday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
